comment: The single record of what this project measured. A figure that is not here is not a figure.
`scripts/numbers-gate.js` reads this file and enforces three rules: no document may restate a value from a
citation whose dataset is below `minimumGroundTruth`; a document that publishes figures must name its sources
with `<!-- figures: citations:<key> -->` and every key must resolve to an artifact that exists; and the gate
fails when it scans fewer than a floor of figure lines, because a check that finds nothing is not a check that
**The veto is the dataset floor, not the `independentValidation` flag.** The flag is a disclosure that is printed
beside the figure; blocking on it would have removed the OWASP score, which is the one figure in this repository
measured on public data with somebody else's labels, and replacing a stated caveat with silence is the failure
The rule underneath all of it: **a number we did not measure is not a comparison.** A figure from someone else's
published documentation has no place in a table of our own results - it reads as a head-to-head result whatever

internal-suite-2026-08.groundTruthSource: two disjoint datasets, counted from the code rather than from a comment: 15 cases carrying 30 ground-truth entries in `benchmark-data.ts`, and 19 fixtures carrying 34 in `benchmark-fixtures.ts`
internal-suite-2026-08.annotationProtocol: single-annotator: the people who wrote the rules wrote the annotations, so the suite is a regression test rather than evidence of quality
internal-suite-2026-08.caveat: **64 issues, below the declared minimum of 100, and the figure that used to stand here was 49.** The 49 was 15 + 34: 15 is the number of CASES in `benchmark-data.ts`, and each case carries two ground-truth entries, so a case count and an issue count were added together and the seam was invisible because the dataset gate counted `id:` strings and the cases are the only `id:` strings in that file. Measured at runtime, the two datasets hold 30 + 34. The figures below stay here as a record of what was measured, not as a claim to publish.

real-bug-fix-commits-2026-10.groundTruthSource: public bug-fix commits, extracted by scripts/extract-real-ground-truth.mjs from benchmarks/real-ground-truth/manifest.json; the line ranges are each commit's own patch hunk headers
real-bug-fix-commits-2026-10.caveat: The ground truth is authored by the humans who wrote the fixes - a line range is the range that fix changed - and each issue carries its repo, sha, commit URL and license so any entry can be checked against GitHub. **The category and severity are NOT authored**: they are inferred from the commit message by rules in the manifest. **The metrics above are measured through `BenchmarkRunner`, which treats a case's `afterContent` as the code under review; for a fix commit that is the BEFORE state, so the before-content is mapped there.**
real-bug-fix-commits-2026-10.metricsNote:
**Measured under both criteria, and the split is the finding.**

  strict   F1 0.0021   the category must equal ours
  overlap  F1 0.2173   the file and the lines must overlap

**So 99% of the 0.0021 was the criterion, not the engine.** `matchGroundTruth` requires `gt.category === result.category`, and on real code those vocabularies do not meet: a human's patch says the lines were wrong and does not say which of our rule families should have caught it. Under overlap the recall is 0.4064 - **the positions are not far off** - and the precision is 0.1483, which is the engine talking too much.

**And what is left is the engine.** Across 688 findings on a hundred real issues the category mix is `style=415 maintainability=226 documentation=32 bug=15`: **2.2% of what this engine reports is a bug**, against ground truth of `bug=246 security=5`. On production code it is a linter for style, and the benchmark asked it to be a bug finder.

**The target is F1 0.68.** At 0.2173 the distance is now explainable rather than mysterious: the criterion is corrected, and what remains is that the engine has to report bugs.
real-bug-fix-commits-2026-10.metricsCriterion: **file plus line overlap** - the criterion a real dataset needs. The stricter criterion (`BenchmarkRunner`'s, which also requires `gt.category === result.category`) gives precision 0.0015, recall 0.004, F1 0.0021 on the same findings. **Both are reported**: the movement between them is the criterion's doing, and any movement after that is the engine's.

owasp-benchmark-1.2.groundTruthSource: the benchmark's own `expectedresults-1.2.csv` (sha256 1809f6a690c6cf7dd6685df6ebe2eef8fe3ca93d19a7ca0ce45987ca4f5d78e1); 1 415 of 2 740 servlets are labelled vulnerable
owasp-benchmark-1.2.caveat: **The labels are the benchmark's; the score is ours.** `scripts/owasp-benchmark.ts` applies the scorecard's own definition - a case counts as flagged if the engine reports at least one flow in its file, and the score is `TPR - FPR` - but it is this project's implementation of that definition and it has never been diffed against OWASP's `BenchmarkUtils` scorecard. The published figure is the union of two engines, reported separately in the artifact: flows 0.6375, rule families 0.3625, union 1.0000 with zero false positives.

cosqa-retrieval.groundTruthSource: CoSQA retrieval test split, `Jun-jie-Huang/CoCLR · data/search/cosqa-retrieval-test-500.json`, sha256 27d3552b2e7dd86cf9f9a0b3c135e6777d4faafa9c29fb1b9b01ece945974ad6; one gold code answer per natural-language query
cosqa-retrieval.caveat: A corpus this project did not author, with the queries and their gold answers fixed before the run. The three columns are the same engine at three stages, so the difference between them is the composition rather than the corpus.

paraphrase-search.groundTruthSource: 99 paraphrased questions over a pinned corpus of 52 files, each with the files that answer it; generated once and frozen before the composition was changed
paraphrase-search.caveat: The questions are generated rather than collected from users, so the absolute level is a statement about this corpus; the ordering between variants is what the run is for. `rerank-deep` reads 0.8384 at 20 against the lexical list's 0.4545, and the ceiling is 0.8889, which is the share of questions the corpus contains an answer for at all.

cross-repo-matrix.groundTruthSource: 49 import pairs read by hand across two real checkouts (pallets/flask importing pallets/werkzeug) plus 73 call paths traced from one repository into the other
cross-repo-matrix.caveat: The pairs are read by hand from two repositories that import each other, which makes them checkable by anyone with the two checkouts; the sample is two repositories, so a recall of 1 is a statement about this pair and not about cross-repository resolution in general.

aacr-bench.groundTruthSource: Alibaba `aacr-bench` (Apache-2.0, public on Hugging Face): 5 pull requests carrying 196 human-recorded review findings, scored by one judge for both reviewers in a single job
aacr-bench.caveat: Both arms run in the same workflow with the same judge, so the comparison is like for like; the corpus is five pull requests, which is enough to compare two tools on the same evidence and not enough to estimate either tool's precision in general.

lca-bug-localization.groundTruthSource: Long Code Arena bug localisation (JetBrains-Research, Apache-2.0): 150 issues, each with the files its fixing commit touched. The three language parts are committed under `benchmarks/lca-parts/`; the merged `benchmarks/lca-bug-localization.json` is produced by the workflow run and is not committed, which is why `scripts/lca-gate.js` can only run inside that workflow.
lca-bug-localization.caveat: **The numbers in this repository do not reproduce from the committed parts, and that is recorded rather than papered over.** The report's table quotes run 0.4673 over 115 of 150 rows, from a run whose merged artifact was never committed; the committed parts aggregate to **0.3955 over all 150 rows** (mean of each row's `map`), with no refusals. The difference is an open defect rather than a rounding: re-running the harness is the only way to say which is current, and until then the table's figure is not backed by anything in the tree.
